author: adrianhollister@infosec.exchange
text: Ransomware does not stop at the live data.  The NCSC has watched it encrypt the connected USB drives and network shares, and compromise cloud backups. The familiar 3-2-1 rule says nothing about any copy being offline.  Three copies, two devices, one offsite can all stay reachable, and one incident can take the lot.  At least one copy needs to be offline or digitally disconnected when idle.  Create-only access on cloud storage gives the write-once effect: ransomware can add a backup but not overwrite the old ones. Rule four gets the least attention: back up often, test the restores. https://www. ncsc.gov.uk/blog-post/offline- backups-in-an-online-world # CyberSecurity # InfoSec # Ransomware

author: adrianhollister@infosec.exchange
text: Ransomware does not stop at the live data.  The NCSC has watched it encrypt the connected USB drives and network shares, and compromise cloud backups. The familiar 3-2-1 rule says nothing about any copy being offline.  Three copies, two devices, one offsite can all stay reachable, and one incident can take the lot.  At least one copy needs to be offline or digitally disconnected when idle.  Create-only access on cloud storage gives the write-once effect: ransomware can add a backup but not overwrite the old ones. Rule four gets the least attention: back up often, test the restores. https://www. ncsc.gov.uk/blog-post/offline- backups-in-an-online-world # CyberSecurity # InfoSec # Ransomware

author: adrianhollister@infosec.exchange
text: Ransomware does not stop at the live data.  The NCSC has watched it encrypt the connected USB drives and network shares, and compromise cloud backups. The familiar 3-2-1 rule says nothing about any copy being offline.  Three copies, two devices, one offsite can all stay reachable, and one incident can take the lot.  At least one copy needs to be offline or digitally disconnected when idle.  Create-only access on cloud storage gives the write-once effect: ransomware can add a backup but not overwrite the old ones. Rule four gets the least attention: back up often, test the restores. https://www. ncsc.gov.uk/blog-post/offline- backups-in-an-online-world # CyberSecurity # InfoSec # Ransomware

Technically - This article details the abuse of the 'text/calendar' MIME type, which is often treated as low-risk by email clients because it is non-executing structured text. Attackers exploit the automatic synchronization workflows of clients like Microsoft Outlook and Gmail to inject lures directly into calendars without user interaction, ensuring persistence even after the source email is deleted. Specific technical applications include the exploitation of a stored XSS vulnerability in Zimbra (CVE-2025-27915) and the use of the EvilTokens toolkit to facilitate OAuth token theft via device code phishing. text: 🚨 Rapid Response | Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server OS Command Injection (CVE-2026-110447) (CVSS 9.2) is a critical OS command injection vulnerability affecting the Collabora Online Built-in CODE Server app for Nextcloud. Exploitation in the wild has been reported, allowing unauthenticated attackers to execute operating system commands. Censys currently detects 19,454 Internet-exposed hosts and 103,350 web properties with the app installed. These figures represent detected installations, not confirmed vulnerable instances. Organizations should upgrade to version 26.4.303 or later, or remove the app. Disabling it is not sufficient. Attackers can use crafted HTTP requests to read specific files from the web application root directory, provided the exact file path is known. author: orlysec@swecyb.com
text: (picussecurity.com) Autonomous Penetration Testing Reveals Detection Gaps in Federal Agency's Active Directory Environment In brief - This article describes how a US federal agency utilized Picus's Autonomous Penetration Testing (APV) and Breach and Attack Simulation (BAS) to identify detection gaps across hundreds of sites within a single Active Directory domain. Technically - This article details an assume-breach, gray-box testing methodology where simulations were scoped to individual site subnets using supplied credentials. While network controls and EDR successfully prevented lateral movement, the testing revealed that credential hashes remained retrievable on hosts where endpoint agents were configured in monitor-only mode. Furthermore, the agency discovered a significant detection failure, with only approximately 10% of sites triggering alerts in the SIEM during simulated attacks. Source: https://www. picussecurity.com/resource/cas e-study/federal-agency-assume-breach-testing-ev

author: adrianhollister@infosec.exchange
text: Ransomware does not stop at the live data.  The NCSC has watched it encrypt the connected USB drives and network shares, and compromise cloud backups. The familiar 3-2-1 rule says nothing about any copy being offline.  Three copies, two devices, one offsite can all stay reachable, and one incident can take the lot.  At least one copy needs to be offline or digitally disconnected when idle.  Create-only access on cloud storage gives the write-once effect: ransomware can add a backup but not overwrite the old ones. Rule four gets the least attention: back up often, test the restores. https://www. ncsc.gov.uk/blog-post/offline- backups-in-an-online-world # CyberSecurity # InfoSec # Ransomware

text: (xbow.com) From Hypothesis to Proof: The Critical Role of Exploitability in Offensive Security In brief - This article argues that vulnerability findings are merely hypotheses until they are proven exploitable in a running system to avoid wasting engineering resources on false positives. Technically - This article discusses the distinction between static code analysis and dynamic exploitability, highlighting how environmental factors like egress policies and metadata services determine the impact of vulnerabilities such as Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). It emphasizes that business logic flaws, such as Insecure Direct Object References (IDOR), cannot be detected by source code analysis alone and require active testing. author: orlysec@swecyb.com
text: (syndis.com) Critical Vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM 800A Refrigeration Controllers Actively Exploited in the Wild In brief - This article warns about critical, actively exploited vulnerabilities in Danfoss AK-SM 800A refrigeration controllers that could lead to food spoilage and operational disruptions. Technically - This article describes vulnerabilities in the web interface of the Danfoss AK-SM 800A control unit that allow attackers to bypass authentication and execute arbitrary commands. These flaws enable unauthorized modification of temperature limits, alarm thresholds, and the triggering of Denial of Service (DoS) attacks. Remediation requires updating to firmware version R4.3.1 and removing the devices from public internet exposure, preferably by implementing VPN-only access. text: (bishopfox.com) AI Security Scoping: Aligning Testing Methods with Risk Decisions in Enterprise AI Deployments In brief - This article discusses the importance of AI security scoping, emphasizing that security must be applied across the entire system ecosystem rather than just the model boundary to make defensible risk decisions. Technically - This article outlines a multi-layered security framework for AI deployments, differentiating between AI penetration testing for technical vulnerabilities in APIs and infrastructure, GenAI architecture reviews for design and data flow analysis, AI red teaming for adversarial behavioral testing (e.g., prompt injection and safeguard bypass), and traditional red teaming for detection and response. It advocates for a full-stack scoping approach that evaluates RAG pipelines, vector store isolation, tool/function execution, identity federation, and the potential for embedding poisoning or cross-tenant data leakage. author: adrianhollister@infosec.exchange
text: Ransomware does not stop at the live data.  The NCSC has watched it encrypt the connected USB drives and network shares, and compromise cloud backups. The familiar 3-2-1 rule says nothing about any copy being offline.  Three copies, two devices, one offsite can all stay reachable, and one incident can take the lot.  At least one copy needs to be offline or digitally disconnected when idle.  Create-only access on cloud storage gives the write-once effect: ransomware can add a backup but not overwrite the old ones. Rule four gets the least attention: back up often, test the restores. https://www. ncsc.gov.uk/blog-post/offline- backups-in-an-online-world # CyberSecurity # InfoSec # Ransomware

text: (recordedfuture.com) TAG-217: AI-Assisted Cyber Attacks on South Korean Financial Institutions Reveal Opportunistic Threat Actor Capabilities In brief - This article details the activities of threat actor TAG-217, who utilized AI-assisted tools to target South Korean financial institutions and explore various other financially motivated attack vectors. Technically - This article describes the use of ARTEX, an open-source AI penetration testing framework, alongside AI models such as Claude Code, DeepSeek, Grok, and Zhipu AI to conduct opportunistic scanning and exploitation. The actor's toolkit included capabilities for stealing cryptocurrency wallet files via the YiiMP platform, exploiting Linux system weaknesses for privilege escalation, and testing mobile vulnerabilities on iOS and Android. To maintain persistence and obfuscate their origin, TAG-217 employed residential proxies, remote access tools, and the synchronization of AI working-memory files across controlled servers. Source:

author: secdb@infosec.exchange
text: 🚨 PwnEscape (CVE-2026-99999) has been identified as a notable vulnerability. In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ipv4: validate checksum_start before completing checksum If a packet with bad checksum metadata gets into the ipv4 stack, skb_checksum_help can corrupt the network header and cause a bunch of mischief. This was discovered and reported by Paulos, and has been reporoduced by others independently since. We really shouldn't allow such packets in, but as a defence in depth measure, let's also check before we complete the checksum. A more complete validation at input is forthcoming, but needs more work. ℹ️ Additional details, advisories and sightings on ZEN SecDB  👉 https:// secdb.nttzen.cloud/cve/detail/ CVE-2026-99999 # InfoSec # PwnEscape # Linux # Kernel # CVE202699999 # NTTDATA # ZENSecDB

author: adrianhollister@infosec.exchange
text: Ransomware does not stop at the live data.  The NCSC has watched it encrypt the connected USB drives and network shares, and compromise cloud backups. The familiar 3-2-1 rule says nothing about any copy being offline.  Three copies, two devices, one offsite can all stay reachable, and one incident can take the lot.  At least one copy needs to be offline or digitally disconnected when idle.  Create-only access on cloud storage gives the write-once effect: ransomware can add a backup but not overwrite the old ones. Rule four gets the least attention: back up often, test the restores. https://www. ncsc.gov.uk/blog-post/offline- backups-in-an-online-world # CyberSecurity # InfoSec # Ransomware

author: orlysec@swecyb.com
text: (recordedfuture.com) TAG-217: AI-Assisted Cyber Attacks on South Korean Financial Institutions Reveal Opportunistic Threat Actor Capabilities In brief - This article details the activities of threat actor TAG-217, who utilized AI-assisted tools to target South Korean financial institutions and explore various other financially motivated attack vectors. Technically - This article describes the use of ARTEX, an open-source AI penetration testing framework, alongside AI models such as Claude Code, DeepSeek, Grok, and Zhipu AI to conduct opportunistic scanning and exploitation. The actor's toolkit included capabilities for stealing cryptocurrency wallet files via the YiiMP platform, exploiting Linux system weaknesses for privilege escalation, and testing mobile vulnerabilities on iOS and Android. To maintain persistence and obfuscate their origin, TAG-217 employed residential proxies, remote access tools, and the synchronization of AI working-memory files across controlled servers. Source:

text: SWANSEA: TGJones confirms closure date for the Quadrant’s old WHSmith TGJones has confirmed to Swansea Bay News that its Swansea store is to close. The shop at the entrance to the Quadrant Shopping Centre was WHSmith until last year. The chain says the closure follows the implementation of its court-approved restructuring plan, and that there will be a closing-down sale first. text: DragonForce Ransomware Profile: From Affiliate Program to Cybercrime Cartel DragonForce is a financially motivated ransomware operation that emerged in August 2023, initially using leaked LockBit 3.0 code and later transitioning to Conti v3-based variants. Operating as a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, they offer affiliates an 80% revenue share and comprehensive management tools. By March 2025, they evolved into a 'cartel' structure, providing white-label services. Their attacks primarily target organizations in the US and UK, spanning multiple sectors including manufacturing, professional services, retail, healthcare, and technology. The group actively recruits developers and reverse engineers while offering specialized data analysis services to help affiliates maximize extortion pressure. Notable incidents include a major MSP breach in May 2025 exploiting SimpleHelp vulnerabilities, cascading compromise across multiple client networks. text: DragonForce Ransomware Profile: From Affiliate Program to Cybercrime Cartel DragonForce is a financially motivated ransomware operation that emerged in August 2023, initially using leaked LockBit 3.0 code and later transitioning to Conti v3-based variants. Operating as a Ransomware-as-a-Service model, they offer affiliates an 80% revenue share and comprehensive management tools. By March 2025, they evolved into a 'cartel' structure, providing white-label services. Their attacks primarily target organizations in the US and UK, spanning multiple sectors including manufacturing, professional services, retail, healthcare, and technology. The group actively recruits developers and reverse engineers while offering specialized data analysis services to help affiliates maximize extortion pressure. Notable incidents include a major MSP breach in May 2025 exploiting SimpleHelp vulnerabilities, cascading compromise across multiple client networks. text: (recordedfuture.com) TAG-217: AI-Assisted Cyber Attacks on South Korean Financial Institutions Reveal Opportunistic Threat Actor Capabilities In brief - This article details the activities of threat actor TAG-217, who utilized AI-assisted tools to target South Korean financial institutions and explore various other financially motivated attack vectors. Technically - This article describes the use of ARTEX, an open-source AI penetration testing framework, alongside AI models such as Claude Code, DeepSeek, Grok, and Zhipu AI to conduct opportunistic scanning and exploitation. The actor's toolkit included capabilities for stealing cryptocurrency wallet files via the YiiMP platform, exploiting Linux system weaknesses for privilege escalation, and testing mobile vulnerabilities on iOS and Android. To maintain persistence and obfuscate their origin, TAG-217 employed residential proxies, remote access tools, and the synchronization of AI working-memory files across controlled servers. Source:

author: orlysec@swecyb.com
text: (bridewell.com) Infostealer Malware Targeting UK Critical National Infrastructure: A Quarter of Escalating Threats and Credential Compromise In brief - This article analyzes infostealer activity targeting UK Critical National Infrastructure (CNI) during Q3 2026, highlighting a trend of credential theft as a precursor to ransomware attacks. Technically - This article details the detection of 20,000 credential sets across 9 UK CNI victims, with 'Generic Stealer' accounting for 32.2% of detections and 18 distinct stealer families identified. It describes the infostealer lifecycle—harvesting browser passwords, session cookies, and VPN/RDP configurations via cracked software or malvertising—and recommends defensive measures such as monitoring LSASS memory access, blocking execution from user-writable folders, and detecting anomalous authentication patterns like impossible-travel logins. Source: https://www. bridewell.com/insights/blogs/d etail/uk-cni-infostealer-threat-report-q3-2026 # Thre

text: Some 315 crypto accounts lost about $102 million last week, drained through hardware implants inside Ledger wallets.  The implant copies the seed phrase as the screen displays it and sends it out over an added LTE module and eSIM.  Joe Grand found the first ones in March, in devices from dodgy online sellers. The newer finds are worse.  They look factory-fitted and are turning up in wallets from authorised resellers, including two bought in person at MediaMarkt stores in Germany.  Buy-direct advice assumed that channel was clean. text: Some 315 crypto accounts lost about $102 million last week, drained through hardware implants inside Ledger wallets.  The implant copies the seed phrase as the screen displays it and sends it out over an added LTE module and eSIM.  Joe Grand found the first ones in March, in devices from dodgy online sellers. Buy-direct advice assumed that channel was clean. author: markwyner@mas.to
text: Y’all! Please, please, please use appropriate passwords. We’re seeing a big spam campaign across the fediverse, using hacked accounts. First, change your fediverse password. Especially if it’s reused elsewhere, short/weak, or really old. Then, here are some simple steps to protect you and your accounts: 1. Never reuse passwords. Use a password manager so you’ll only have to remember one password. 2. Make sure your passwords are secure. They should be 12+ characters with at least one capital letter and one special character. Good password managers have a generator built-in. 3. Set-up multi-factor authentication (MFA/2FA). 4. Use passkeys wherever possible. If you need help, ask someone. Folks who know will help. # Passwords # Security # InfoSec # OpSec # 2FA # MFA # Mastodon # Fediverse # FediTips # MastodonTips

author: markwyner@mas.to
text: Y’all! Please, please, please use appropriate passwords. We’re seeing a big spam campaign across the fediverse, using hacked accounts. First, change your fediverse password. Especially if it’s reused elsewhere, short/weak, or really old. Then, here are some simple steps to protect you and your accounts: 1. Never reuse passwords. Use a password manager so you’ll only have to remember one password. 2. Make sure your passwords are secure. They should be 12+ characters with at least one capital letter and one special character. Good password managers have a generator built-in. 3. Set-up multi-factor authentication (MFA/2FA). 4. Use passkeys wherever possible. If you need help, ask someone. Folks who know will help. # Passwords # Security # InfoSec # OpSec # 2FA # MFA # Mastodon # Fediverse # FediTips # MastodonTips

author: PH4NTXMOFFICIAL@defcon.social
text: Inside PH4NTXM: #54 App Airlock Applications deserve boundaries too. PH4NTXM App Airlock launches installed applications and custom commands inside a disposable offline environment, with a private desktop, isolated home and an explicit RAM workspace. No direct network access. No shared host home directory. No automatic access to mounted drives. Selected files are copied into the workspace. Applications can work on them and save results there, while originals remain unchanged. Execution must stop before results can be explicitly exported, without overwriting existing files. Resource limits and fail-closed startup checks apply throughout. Closing the Airlock clears its temporary workspace. This is process isolation using the host kernel, rather than a separate virtual machine. Applications that require internet or unavailable host services may not function, and exported files still need review before use. # ph4ntxm # linux # debian # os # live # privacy # security # opsec # infosec # res
